payload.field_feedback:
ASKED FIRST, before any gathering, and the owner answered: "I feel like we are currently making mistakes that v1 didn't make IN THE END. But it might have also made the same mistakes EARLIER. So check out the guidance in v1 and whatever you can learn from that, put it into your guidance. Other than that, I think everything is in notes."

That is a precise piece of feedback, not a complaint: it names a hypothesis AND its test. If v1 made the same mistakes early and stopped, the stopping is encoded in v1's guidance - so the lessons are recoverable without re-learning them.

I acted on it inside this retro rather than deferring: read v1's method/rigor/systematic/checklist.md and method/prompts/contract.md. The hypothesis holds. Five concrete items v1 carries and v2 does not are listed under process_stale; the most important one is a direct antidote to the failure mechanism the owner has been complaining about all afternoon.

SECOND PIECE OF FIELD FEEDBACK, delivered as a ruling during the retro: the lane's read/write tools must reach EVERY folder, not only the product - "they should log onto the product, but they can go everywhere." See notes_drained; it closes the oldest unserved demand in the log.

The rest of the field feedback is the whole of today, already in notes: the untappable card, the missing hosted brief, the card that was a wall of text instead of a link, the controls that belonged in the page, and three hand-rolled workarounds.
payload.notes_drained:
Inbox 6 at retro start, one more captured DURING the retro (the every-folder ruling), 7 dispositioned, inbox 0.

PULLED INTO i12 (5): the read/search surface (the iteration's central thrust, with its counter-argument recorded so the fix is not one-sided); the se_run fence hole, re-framed after the owner's ruling to target INVISIBILITY rather than workarounds; required-arg enforcement at dispatch; the model-quality/under-building question, now partly answered by v1's guidance; and the every-folder scope ruling, flagged as SUPERSEDING the plan's older "declared roots, never arbitrary" items in i3/i4 - the owner confirms that supersession at kickoff rather than me assuming it.

ROUTED, NOT PULLED (2): the board's new-tab-per-start goes to i9-board-rounds, where board work belongs, carrying its diagnosis and the honest limit that no shell open command can refocus an existing tab. The one-representation/mutual-invalidation design goes to the next phone iteration, per the owner's own "we can do this in the next iteration".

ONE FOLLOW-UP THE DRAIN CREATED, and it is the kind a drain should create: the last note MIXED a design request with a shipped BUG. I minted se.raid-hosted-page-claims-a-bless-it-did-not-land so the defect cannot travel as a feature request - the hosted page reports 'Blessed' on a relay 200 even when the engine bound nothing, which is the silent-success class the whitelist law exists to kill.

REJECTED: none. Every note earned a home.
payload.call_log_mined:
4131 calls total, 154 failures - a 3.7% refusal rate. The interesting numbers are not the totals.

THE MOST-USED PRODUCT TOOL IS THE ONE WITH THE WORST ERGONOMICS. se_file_patch: 645 calls, by far the most-used product tool (se_file_read 210, se_file_write 136, se_file_search 108, se_file_list 18) - and it applies exactly ONE edit per call, while se_set_apply batches ledger ops freely. It is also the top-failing product tool: 28 failures, more than any other. So the single highest-traffic path is the one that cannot batch and fails most often. That is not a preference for batch mode, it is a measurement.

THE se_help MISSES CLUSTER, AND THE CLUSTER WAS NEVER SERVED. Walking all 17: the demand signal has WORKED for most categories - a run lane was missed on 2026-07-23 and se_run exists; a note lane was missed and se_note exists; git unstage was missed and restore --staged was allowlisted; canvas ops were missed and se_set_apply gained them. EXACTLY ONE CATEGORY WAS NEVER BUILT: reading and searching. 2026-07-23 08:45 "search deliverable source files pattern grep"; 2026-07-23 16:00 "read se-v2-design.md from the owner's working folder (outside the v2 root)"; 2026-07-23 17:39 "read another repo v1 method files"; 2026-07-24 07:28 "read v1 files method engage retro - declared-roots search scope is only planned for i3"; 2026-07-24 07:49 "read notes inbox list drain"; 2026-07-25 12:58 "read a large file in parts, offset limit chunk, search with surrounding context". SIX MISSES ACROSS THREE DAYS, one capability, never built - while every other category got built within days. The demand signal is not broken; this particular demand was simply never picked up.

AND IT COLLIDES WITH A STANDING LAW. The porting law requires consulting v1 AND the design document on every piece of work. The lane can reach neither: v1 is outside the root, and se-v2-design.md is 132k chars with no chunked read. So the process MANDATES two sources the tools cannot open. That is a designed-in contradiction, and it is the leading explanation for i8d's three design-doc-to-build losses. Note that v1 IS readable with the native tools - I read its checklist and contract during this very retro in two calls - which is exactly why the workaround pressure exists.

CLAUSES: 111 of 154 failures carry NO clause (72%), almost all se.run non-zero exits, which legitimately have none. Of the clauseful 43, the top three are SE-C-046 (8, the toll's update field), SE-C-064 (6) and SE-C-030 (6). Nothing dominates; no refusal is systematically fighting the agent. The clauseless majority is a known hygiene item, not news.

TOOL-NAME DOUBLE-COUNTING: the log carries both se.run/se_run and se.help/se_help, and se_deliverable_* alongside se_file_* from before a rename. Harmless for ranking, but it means any automated retro query undercounts unless it normalizes - worth fixing when the log aggregation is next touched.
payload.waste_leads:
THREE HAND-ROLLED WORKAROUNDS IN ONE ITERATION, each traceable to a specific missing affordance rather than to impatience: ctor-sweep.mjs (six mechanical edits, because se_file_patch has no batch mode); design-card-shape.mjs (reading the design document, because se_file_read cannot chunk); and the announce/poll harness (because an iteration cannot exercise its own build through the live surface). The owner's ruling reframed these: working around a gap is legal, hiding it is not - now se.law-workaround-then-record-the-gap.

REWORK, and this is the expensive one: the release gate was filled and offered THREE TIMES. Once with a card that was a wall of text, once after the one-line-link correction, once after the controls moved into the page. Each round cost a full evidence fill plus an owner round-trip. ROOT CAUSE, and it is not the card: all three corrections were already ruled in se-v2-design §11 - "ntfy carries the notification (click URL = page + #key)", "the SAME rich handover HTML (v1-style drill-down, BLESS CONTROLS) on desk and phone - not an editorially compressed brief" - and §16 had already closed the only technical blocker (CORS on the ntfy fetch, VERIFIED PASS 2026-07-21). Every correction the owner made was recovering a ruling the document already contained. THREE OWNER ROUNDS SPENT RE-DERIVING WHAT WAS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN.

WASTED VERIFICATION: I believed a search result that was answering a different question (se_file_search coerced a wrong arg name and searched for the literal word 'undefined'), concluded the engine had a bug, and wrote a note asserting it. Both the conclusion and the note had to be retracted. A refusal would have cost one turn; a confident wrong answer cost four.

NOT WASTE, recorded so it is not mistaken for it: the two live probes (transport 7/7, chain 10/10) and the SP1 crypto spike each caught a real defect before it reached the owner's device - SP1 alone caught two crypto layout errors that would have failed silently in a browser while every server-side check stayed green.
payload.process_stale:
THE STANDING CHECK, run against v1 rather than against the literature, because the owner's field feedback pointed there and v1 is the closest comparable system that already solved this.

VERDICT: v2's machine is STALE against v1's checklist in five places, and one of them is the direct antidote to this week's failures.

1. THE BIG ONE - PRIOR ART ON THE REQUIREMENT SET. v1's M2 carries a check v2 has nowhere: "prior art checked - the requirement set positioned against best practice; misses added or recorded", with the method spelled out as "what does the standard checklist for this kind of deliverable demand that the set is MISSING?" v2 checks requirements for verifiability, tracing and coverage - all internal properties - and never once asks whether the SET is missing something its sources already ruled. That is exactly where i8d lost the bless controls: the design document said the page carries them, my register said the page carries the brief, and every downstream gate faithfully checked the build against the register. The loss was invisible from M3 onward. v1's check would have caught it AT the requirements gate.

2. STATE OF THE ART ON THE IDEA, at M1. v1: "state of the art checked - prior art scanned; the idea positioned against it". v2 runs a state-of-the-art check only at the retro, on the PROCESS. The product idea is never positioned.

3. THE ARCHITECTURE DIAGRAM IS A HARD-RULE KILLER IN v1. "architecture model ready for diagram review (killer, HARD RULE): the chosen architecture view exists, names the blocks the build will fill, shows their relationships or boundaries, and records the placement rationale. The OWNER REVIEWS THAT DIAGRAM here." v2's gate_architecture is prose - i8d's had no diagram at all, and the owner adjudicated a wall of text. There is even a standing owner rule that asking about a model REQUIRES a clickable rendered link.

4. VIEW SELECTION IS EXPLICIT IN v1: "model kinds picked from the registry, each with the question it answers; REJECTED KINDS RECORDED; two models is the default budget." v2 has no view-selection step, so the choice of what to draw is never made or defended.

5. MODELS-ADHERED-TO IS LINTED IN v1, not merely asserted: "the conformance/sky-fall lint enforces it". In v2 it is a sentence I write about my own work.

SEPARATELY, ON ADJUDICATION - worth the owner's attention rather than my decision. v1's contract rule 3 is STRICTER than v2's practice: the agent may bless only NON-killer reviews itself; a killer gate always reaches the user as a pager, and "a blanket 'keep going' or 'continue' is NOT permission to bless a killer." v2's delegated adjudication is blanket by comparison - i8d self-blessed nine gates including every killer. That is legitimate, because the owner granted it explicitly and wanted an unattended run. But it means v2 currently has NO structural backstop on killers, where v1 had one by default, and the quality complaints of the last two days are precisely about killers that passed. The retro's job is to surface that, not to settle it.

Also stale, mechanically: the plan's "declared roots, never arbitrary" items are superseded by the owner's every-folder ruling; and the porting law that mandates reading v1 and the design document is unenforceable while the lane cannot open either.
